 ORDER
(Per: Ms. Kumkum Rani, President):
This appeal has been directed against the impugned judgment
and order dated 23.01.2026 passed by learned District Consumer
Disputes Redressal Commission, Dehradun (hereinafter to be referred
1
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others

as "The District Commission") in consumer complaint bearing
No. DC/49/CC/393/2021, styled as Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan Vs. Go
Digit General Insurance Limited and others, whereby the consumer
complaint filed by the appellant / complainant was dismissed.
2. The facts giving rise to the present appeal, in brief, are as such
that the appellant / complainant is the registered owner of vehicle
(Mahindra and Mahindra XUV 300 W4 PET MT WP) bearing
registration No. UK16-C-3489, which was insured with respondent
No. 1 / opposite party No. 1 for the period from 07.04.2019 to
06.03.2020 at an IDV of Rs. 7,50,500/-. During the currency of the
insurance policy, the insured vehicle met with an accident in the
evening of 02.03.2020 at Village Kachta, Gangro, Jaindo Motor Road,
Tehsil Kalsi, District Dehradun, F.I.R. whereof was lodged with the
Revenue Police, Kalsi by one Sh. Pradeep Singh Chauhan. In the
accident, the insured vehicle was completely damaged. The intimation
of the accident was immediately conveyed by the complainant to the
insurance company and claim for indemnification of loss was submitted
with the insurance company. The insurance company appointed
Sh. Himanshu Sharma as investigator, who demanded certain
documents from the complainant, which were duly provided by the
complainant through letter dated 01.06.2020. The insurance company,
however vide letter dated 02.09.2020 repudiated the complainant's
claim on the ground of delay in intimation; misrepresentation of facts
& violation of driver's clause of policy schedule and over-seating. The
insurance company has repudiated the claim on false grounds. Thus,
alleging deficiency in service on the part of the insurance company,
consumer complaint was submitted by the complainant before the
District Commission.
2
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others
3. The respondents / opposite parties (insurance company) filed
written statement before the District Commission and pleaded that the
complainant has not approached the District Commission with clean
hands. The intimation of the accident dated 02.03.2020, was given to
the insurance company on 05.03.2020, i.e., after three days' of the
occurrence. During the course of investigation, it transpired that at the
time of accident, Sh. Pradeep Singh Chauhan was not driving the
insured vehicle and as per the report of the investigator, the insured
vehicle was being driven by Sh. Sandeep Chauhan, the real brother of
the insured, who was injured in the accident. The driving license of
Sh. Sandeep Chauhan was not provided by the complainant and
Sh. Pradeep Singh Chauhan, another brother of the insured, was
projected as driver of the vehicle. The report of the accident was given
to the Revenue Police Chowki, Gagaro, Tehsil Kalsi by one
Sh. Jawahar Singh. There were six persons sitting in the vehicle at the
time of accident, out of whom, three died and three sustained injuries.
Since the complainant failed to respond to the queries raised by the
insurance company, his claim was repudiated through letter dated
30.06.2020. There has not been any deficiency in service on the part of
the insurance company and the consumer complaint is liable to be
dismissed.
4. The District Commission, after hearing learned counsel for the
parties and after taking into consideration the material available on
record, dismissed the consumer complaint vide impugned judgment
and order dated 23.01.2026. Feeling aggrieved by the impugned
judgment and order, the complainant has come up in this appeal and
filed the same as an appellant.
3
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others
5. We have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the
record.
6. There is no dispute with regard to the insurance of the subject
vehicle and the same having met with an accident during the
subsistence of the insurance policy. So far as the plea of delayed
intimation of accident raised by the insurance company is concerned,
Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
Om Prakash Vs. Reliance General
Insurance and another
reported in 2017 0 Supreme (SC) 977, has
held that it is true that the owner of the vehicle has to intimate the
insurer immediately after the theft of the vehicle, but this condition
should not bar settlement of genuine claims. Relevant paragraph
No. 11 of the aforesaid judgment is reproduced below:
"11. It is common knowledge that a person
 who lost his vehicle may not
 straightaway go to the Insurance
 Company to claim compensation. At
 first, he will make efforts to trace the
 vehicle. It is true that the owner has to
 intimate the insurer immediately after
 the theft of the vehicle. However, this
 condition should not bar settlement of
 genuine claims particularly when the
 delay in intimation or submission of
 documents is due to unavoidable
 circumstances. The decision of the
 insurer to reject the claim has to be
 based on valid grounds. Rejection of
 the claims on purely technical grounds
 in a mechanical manner will result in
 loss of confidence of policy-holders in
 the insurance industry. If the reason
 for delay in making a claim is
 satisfactorily explained, such a claim
4
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others

 cannot be rejected on the ground of
 delay. It is also necessary to state here
 that it would not be fair and reasonable
 to reject genuine claims which had
 already been verified and found to be
 correct by the Investigator. The
 condition regarding the delay shall not
 be a shelter to repudiate the insurance
 claims which have been otherwise
 proved to be genuine. It needs no
 emphasis that the
Consumer Protection
 Act
aims at providing better protection
 of the interest of consumers. It is a
 beneficial legislation that deserves
 liberal construction. This laudable
 object should not be forgotten while
 considering the claims made under the
 Act."
7. Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of
Gurshinder Singh Vs.
Shriram General Insurance Company Limited and another
reported in 2020 0 Supreme (SC) 70, has laid down that it would be a
hyper technical view if the claim is denied merely on the ground that
there is some delay in intimating the insurance company about the
occurrence of theft. Relevant paragraph No. 18 of the judgment is
reproduced below:
"18. We concur with the view taken in the
 case of
Om Prakash
(supra), that in
 such a situation if the claimant is
 denied the claim merely on the ground
 that there is some delay in intimating
 the insurance company about the
 occurrence of the theft, it would be
 taking a hyper technical view.
We
 find, that this Court in
Om Prakash
(supra) has rightly held that it would
 not be fair and reasonable to reject
 genuine claims which had already
5
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others

 been verified and found to be correct
 by the investigator."
8. It is true that in the case in hand pertains to accident of the insured
vehicle and not theft thereof, but the insurance company has not raised
any doubt about the genuineness of the claim and there is no case of the
insurance company that the insured vehicle did not meet with an
accident. It would not be out of place to mention here that Sh. Adhar
Sharma, surveyor & loss assessor, appointed by the insurance company,
in his motor survey report dated 25.06.2020, copy whereof is Paper
Nos. 22 to 25, has clearly stated that this type of accident is possible
and the damages seem to be authentic. Thus, the ground of delay
intimation taken by the insurance company for repudiation of the
genuine claim of the complainant, has no substance.
9. So far as another plea taken by the insurance company that at the
time of accident, Sh. Sandeep Chauhan was driving the subject vehicle
and not Sh. Pradeep Singh Chauhan, as alleged by the complainant, it
is pertinent to mention here that the issue as to who was driving the
vehicle at the time of accident has no more value, in the current
scenario. The reason being that firstly, the above-mentioned surveyor
in his motor survey report has clearly mentioned the name of the driver
as Sh. Sandeep Chauhan S/o Sh. Sultan Singh, as per police diary.
Secondly, the same insurance company in entered into compromise in
M.A.C.P. No. 14 of 2020; Sh. Virendra Singh and others Vs. Sh. Jaipal
Singh and others & M.A.C.P. No. 27 of 2020; Sh. Geetam Singh and
others Vs. Sh. Jaipal Singh and others and on the basis of the
compromise arrived between the claimants of the above claim petitions
and the insurance company, the above claim petitions were decided by
learned Civil Judge Senior Division, Vikasnagar, Dehradun in National
6
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others

Lok Adalat vide order dated 13.05.2023, copy of the orders have been
submitted as Paper Nos. 26 and 27. Thus, the ground of the driving
license of the driver driving the vehicle at the time of accident, not
holding valid and effective driving license, has become redundant.
10. So far as the issue of overloading of the vehicle at the time of the
accident is concerned, the total seating capacity of the vehicle was five
and as per the insurance company, there were six persons sitting in the
vehicle at the time of the accident. Even if the stand taken by the
insurance company is accepted, then also merely be sitting of one extra
person beyond the permitted seating capacity of the vehicle, it can not
be said that the vehicle was overloaded. Even otherwise, as stated
above, the surveyor appointed by the insurance company has found the
accident as genuine and has not assigned the alleged overloading as the
cause of the accident.
11. In view of above discussion, we arrive at a definite conclusion
that there was clear-cut deficiency in service on the part of the insurance
company, by repudiating the genuine and bonafide claim of the
complainant.
12. So far as quantum is concerned, the vehicle was insured at an
IDV of Rs. 7,50,500/-. The surveyor in his report has assessed the loss
to the tune of Rs. 6,59,723/- on repair basis and has worked out the net
liability of the insurance company with Add on cover to the tune of
above sum of Rs. 6,59,723/-. The amount so assessed by the surveyor
comes more than 75% of the IDV, hence it can safely be said that the
case in hand falls under the category of "total loss", as has rightly been
claimed by the complainant in the consumer complaint. The surveyor
7
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others

has not assessed the value of the salvage, but has valued the
depreciation as Rs. 1,22,653.38/- towards depreciation. Since the case
falls under the category of "total loss", hence the same is to be settled
on total loss basis. In our view, the value of the salvage should be taken
as Rs. 1,00,000/- and the said amount is to be deducted from the IDV
of the vehicle. In addition thereto, an amount of Rs. 1,000/- towards
excess is also be deducted. This way, the total amount of Rs. 1,01,000/-
should be deducted from the IDV of the vehicle and the complainant is
to be held entitled to balance sum of Rs. 6,49,500/- (Rs. 7,50,500/-
minus Rs. 1,01,000/-). Since the insurance company has wrongly
repudiated the claim of the complainant, thereby committing deficiency
in service, hence on the said amount, the complainant is also entitled to
interest @7% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint,
i.e., 26.02.2021 till payment and Rs. 10,000/- towards litigation
expenses.
13. For the reasons aforesaid, the appeal deserves to be allowed and
the impugned judgment and order passed by the District Commission
is liable to be set aside and the consumer complaint is fit to be allowed
in the above terms.
14. Appeal is allowed. Impugned judgment and order dated
23.01.2026 passed by the District Commission is set aside. Consumer
complaint bearing No. DC/49/CC/393/2021 is allowed and the
respondents - insurance company is directed to pay compensation of
Rs. 6,49,500/- to the appellant / complainant together with interest
@7% p.a. from the date of filing of the consumer complaint, i.e.,
26.02.2021 till payment and Rs. 10,000/- towards litigation expenses.
8
SC/5/FA/20/2026 Sh. Jaipal Singh Chauhan 10.09.2026
 Versus
 Go Digit General Insurance Limited and others
15. A copy of this Order be provided to all the parties free of cost as
mandated by the
Consumer Protection Act, 1986
/ 2019. The Order be
uploaded forthwith on the website of the Commission for the perusal of
the parties. A copy of this Order be sent to the concerned District
Commission for record and necessary information.
16. File be consigned to record room along with a copy of this Order.
(Ms. Kumkum Rani)
 President
